legacy_root.question: Between the MCP protocol revisions currently in the wild, which capabilities became mandatory, which remain optional, and which clients implement which revision — the matrix that decides what an MCP adapter may assume?
legacy_root.headline: No named feature capability on ServerCapabilities or ClientCapabilities is JSON-Schema-required in any of the five published schema directories ['2024-11-05', '2025-03-26', '2025-06-18', '2025-11-25', '2026-07-28']. What became mandatory is session machinery: initialize + notifications/initialized through 2025-11-25, then server/discover in 2026-07-28 (initialize removed). Feature flags stay optional. An adapter may assume the handshake of the negotiated revision, not tools/resources/prompts.

became_mandatory.caveat: Mandatory for handshake-era sessions. Absent in 2026-07-28 schema (replaced by server/discover).
Paired with initialize; absent once initialize is removed.
Servers MUST implement it. Clients MAY skip the call and send RPCs directly, handling UnsupportedProtocolVersionError.

introduced_then_removed_from_core.core_status_2026-07-28: absent (moved to extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks per changelog)

adapter_may_assume: A negotiated handshake-era session speaks initialize (mandatory) and may omit every feature capability.
A negotiated 2026-07-28 server implements server/discover (mandatory) and carries protocol version in _meta; feature capabilities remain optional.
Do not assume tools, resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation, or tasks without reading the peer's capabilities object (or 2026 extensions map).
Do not treat TypeScript SDK LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION=2025-11-25 as the version a default client actually negotiates (DEFAULT_NEGOTIATED_PROTOCOL_VERSION=2025-03-26).
